project: Des Moines Insider - organic recovery and the volume we measured
description: Continues prd-seo.json (SEO-001 through SEO-020). Two inputs. First, a live audit of desmoinesinsider.com run as GPTBot on 2026-08-31, two days after the SEO-001..016 batch shipped: entity prerendering renders correctly but covers only a quarter of what it should, and three things are broken that were not broken before. Second, a Keyword Planner pull of the 377-term seed list in docs/seo/keyword-research/, joined back to route status in keyword-opportunities.csv. The joined data is what orders phase 2: it says the largest soft volume is on routes that already exist and serve the homepage. Phase 1 is defects on live URLs. Phase 2 is content against measured demand. Phase 2 does not pay off until phase 1 lands, for the same reason it did not last time.

baselines.method: curl as GPTBot and Googlebot against production; PostgREST probe of the gsc_* tables; Keyword Planner export joined to the seed classification
baselines.entityPagesServingOwnTitleAndJsonLd: CORRECTED 2026-08-31: 267 of 1127 prerendered per the build log. The original '3 of 3 sampled' was a biased sample - all three sat near the front of the render order. Events 525/525 and restaurants 335/477 ship as an SPA shell. See SEO-027.

userStories.title: Every hub 308s away from the URL its own canonical declares
userStories.description: As Googlebot consolidating duplicate URLs, I am told the canonical is /restaurants and then handed a 308 when I fetch it. Measured on production 2026-08-31: /restaurants returns 308 to /restaurants/, /restaurants/ returns 200, and the 200 page's canonical tag reads https://desmoinesinsider.com/restaurants. Same for /events, /things-to-do, /attractions and /playgrounds. The declared canonical is a URL that redirects, on the five pages that carry most of the site's impressions. SEO-004 shipped a trailing-slash 301 in functions/_middleware.ts with 23 checks and it is inert in production: the asset bypass near functions/_middleware.ts:246 calls context.next() before the trailing-slash branch at :253 is reached, and Cloudflare Pages then adds the slash itself because the prerender pass writes directory-style output. The redirect behaviour is measured. The cause is inferred from Pages' documented directory handling plus that ordering, and local dist/ was stale at audit time, so CONFIRM THE EMITTED FILENAME before choosing a fix.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm first, from a real build, whether scripts/prerender.mjs writes dist/restaurants/index.html or dist/restaurants.html. The fix depends on the answer and the audit could not verify it.

Pick ONE direction and make every signal agree with it. Either make prerender emit <route>.html so Pages serves the unslashed form directly and the existing canonicals stay correct, or move to slashed URLs and rewrite every canonical. Do not do half of each.

DO NOT move the trailing-slash check ahead of the asset bypass without also changing the output shape. Middleware 301 /x/ -> /x combined with Pages 308 /x -> /x/ is an infinite redirect loop on the site's five most important pages.

After deploy, for each of /restaurants /events /things-to-do /attractions /playgrounds: the canonical URL must return 200 directly, with no redirect hop, and the page's own canonical tag must equal the URL that was fetched.

Add a test that asserts the direction end to end rather than in isolation. The existing functions/__tests__/middleware-trailing-slash.test.mjs passes today while production does the opposite, so a unit test over trailingSlashRedirect() is not sufficient evidence and must not be the only check.
Correct the stale flag in prd-seo.json: SEO-004 is marked passes:true and is not working in production. Set it back to false or record why it should stay closed.
userStories.notes: Highest priority in the file. It is a signal-level defect on the highest-impression pages, the fix is config-level, and it was introduced by the SEO-001 prerender change rather than being long-standing. Verified 2026-08-31 with curl -A Googlebot against production. DONE 2026-08-31. Confirmed from a real build that prerender emitted dist/<route>/index.html, and changed it to flat dist/<route>.html via the new scripts/prerender-output.mjs - the direction that leaves every existing canonical and sitemap entry correct, against the alternative of rewriting them all and moving already-indexed URLs. The middleware redirect stays disabled and is now redundant rather than merely off. Verified: build emits restaurants.html / events.html / things-to-do.html / attractions.html / playgrounds.html flat, and check-canonical-url-shape.mjs exits 0 across 36 routes. That gate failed on its first run against a REAL pre-existing defect it was not written for - /visitors-guide shipped with no canonical tag at all, on production too - which is the argument for comparing artifacts rather than unit-testing a function. Fixed in src/pages/VisitorsGuide.tsx, along with a JSON-LD url field that emitted an empty string into the prerendered HTML.

userStories.title: Six hub routes still serve the homepage to crawlers that do not run JavaScript
userStories.description: As an AI search crawler, /outdoors, /music, /sports, /breweries, /best-of and /getting-around all return 200 with zero JSON-LD, the homepage title 'Des Moines Insider | Events, Restaurants and What to Do in Des Moines', and the same 4,042 words of homepage body. This is the exact defect SEO-001 fixed for the ~1,070 entity pages, still live on six hubs, because they are absent from the 44 routes in scripts/prerender-routes.mjs. It matters more than the count suggests: the joined keyword data puts 118,400 monthly searches on the /outdoors cluster alone across 19 terms, 19 of 19 returning volume, at competition index 1 to 3, and /music and /sports carry the venue-logistics and Iowa Cubs clusters.
acceptanceCriteria: Add all six routes to PRERENDER_ROUTES in scripts/prerender-routes.mjs.
They must pass the same strict per-page validation SEO-001 built. A route that renders as the homepage shell must fail the build rather than be published, which is the whole point of that gate.
Verify after deploy with curl -A GPTBot: each of the six returns its own <title>, at least one application/ld+json block, and body text that is not the homepage's.
Emit a schema type that matches what each page is, not a generic WebPage. /outdoors and /breweries are ItemList over Place; /music and /sports are ItemList over Event where events exist.
Do not add editorial content in this story. Prerendering the shell is the defect; content depth for /outdoors is SEO-024 and depends on this landing first.
userStories.notes: Cheapest technical win left. The routes exist, the renderer exists, the validation exists, and six entries are missing from one array. Measured 2026-08-31.

userStories.title: Search Console sync has never been scheduled, so nothing above is measurable
userStories.description: As the person deciding what to build next, I have no ongoing organic data. supabase/functions/gsc-sync-data/index.ts writes gsc_keyword_performance, gsc_page_performance and gsc_properties. All three tables exist and all three return [] to the anon key, and no cron schedules the function anywhere in supabase/migrations/, supabase-cron-setup.sql or supabase/config.toml. The [] could be RLS hiding rows from anon rather than empty tables, so that part is unproven, but the absent schedule is not: the sync only runs when somebody triggers it by hand. Every number in docs/seo-plan-2026-08-28.md is a one-off manual export, and src/components/admin/SearchTrafficDashboard sits on top of it.
acceptanceCriteria: Schedule gsc-sync-data on a daily cron following the pattern already used by the other scheduled functions in supabase-cron-setup.sql. Match the existing CRON_SECRET convention rather than inventing a new auth path.
Establish whether the gsc_* tables are actually empty or merely RLS-hidden from anon, and say which in the progress log. The remedy differs.

After the first successful run, record the real current numbers in the progress log: clicks, impressions, CTR and average position for the trailing 28 days, plus per-hub rows for the five pages in SEO-021.
Backfill as much history as the Search Console API will return in one pass, so there is a before-and-after around the 2026-08-29 ship date rather than only an after.
The dashboard must render real rows after the sync. If it does not, that is a bug in this story, not a follow-up.
userStories.notes: Sequenced into phase 1 because it is the instrument, not the experiment. Without it, SEO-021 and SEO-022 can only be verified by hand with curl, and phase 2 has no feedback at all.

userStories.title: /outdoors is the largest soft-competition cluster we measured and it has no page
userStories.description: As somebody searching for trails and parks around Des Moines, I get the CVB or a state-parks site, because our /outdoors route serves the homepage. The Keyword Planner join in docs/seo/keyword-research/keyword-opportunities.csv puts 118,400 monthly searches across 19 outdoors terms with a 19 of 19 hit rate, nearly all Low competition: grays lake park des moines at the 50,000 bucket with competition index 3, ledges state park at 50,000 index 1, raccoon river valley trail at 5,000, best bike trails des moines, best hiking near des moines, dog parks des moines and high trestle trail parking at 500 each. This cluster does not appear anywhere in docs/seo-plan-2026-08-28.md. It was found by the volume pull.
acceptanceCriteria: Depends on SEO-022. Do not start until /outdoors prerenders as itself.
Build /outdoors as a real guide, not a filtered grid. Editorial depth in the range the plan set for the other hubs, and an internal link count in the competition's range rather than a third of it.

Cover the specific entities the volume pull named, each as its own section or child page with a Place or TouristAttraction schema: Gray's Lake Park, Ledges State Park, High Trestle Trail, Raccoon River Valley Trail, Neal Smith Trail, Great Western Trail, Big Creek State Park, Jester Park.
Answer the logistics the queries actually ask: parking, trailheads, distance from downtown, whether dogs are allowed, and what is open in winter. That is the part the CVB does not publish.
Cross-link both directions with /playgrounds, which is already the best-positioned module on the site and shares the same audience.
Read the cluster rows in docs/seo/keyword-research/keyword-opportunities.csv before writing, and target the terms that are actually there rather than assumed ones.
userStories.notes: Volume figures are Keyword Planner buckets (50 / 500 / 5,000 / 50,000) from an account with no active ad spend, so they are order-of-magnitude only and no traffic forecast should be derived from them. The competition index is paid competition, which is a proxy for commercial contest and not for organic difficulty.

userStories.title: The suburb pSEO slugs are defined, the routes resolve, and they serve the homepage
userStories.description: As an Ankeny or West Des Moines resident searching for restaurants in my own town, I get a 200 and the Des Moines Insider homepage. scripts/pseo-slugs.txt defines 244 slugs and sitemap-pseo.xml publishes 16. The suburb cluster is the largest volume block in the whole keyword file: 157,450 monthly searches, 71 of 90 terms returning volume, almost entirely Low competition. 'restaurants in west des moines iowa' sits at the 50,000 bucket with competition index 14, and /restaurants/west-des-moines is a defined slug that today returns the homepage to GPTBot. The whole Ankeny set is at the 5,000 bucket. This is content missing behind routes that already work, not engineering.
acceptanceCriteria: Depends on SEO-021 and SEO-022. The plan's own warning applies: scaling pSEO before hub quality is fixed multiplies a thin template.

Publish the suburb pages for the towns the volume pull actually rewarded. Ankeny, West Des Moines, Urbandale, Waukee, Johnston, Altoona and Grimes returned volume; check the rows before committing to a list.

Do NOT publish the nine neighborhood slugs that returned no volume at all: Court Avenue, Valley Junction, Beaverdale, Sherman Hill, Drake, Ingersoll, Highland Park, Merle Hay and Gray's Lake as a dining area. East Village and downtown returned 5,000 each and are worth building; the rest are template multiplication with no measured demand behind them.
Each published page must clear the same strict prerender validation as every other route and must carry schema matching its type.
Add every published page to sitemap-pseo.xml and link it from the parent hub in both directions.

Blank volume in Keyword Planner is suppression, not proof of zero demand - the playground and kids terms all came back blank while Search Console measures that module at 6,706 impressions ranking 6 to 7. Use the blanks to deprioritise, never as evidence to delete a page that already ranks.
userStories.notes: The largest single volume block in docs/seo/keyword-research/keyword-opportunities.csv, and the cheapest, because the slugs and routes already exist.

userStories.title: The restaurant head terms are 50,000-volume at competition index 11 and we sit at position 52
userStories.description: As somebody searching 'best restaurants in des moines', I do not see the site that has 408 restaurant pages and 180,254 impressions. docs/seo-plan-2026-08-28.md writes off all nine core head terms together. The volume pull says that was right for two of them and wrong for two others: 'des moines restaurants' and 'best restaurants in des moines' are both 50,000-bucket at competition index 11, while 'things to do in des moines' and 'des moines attractions' are the same 50,000 bucket at index 87. Same volume, eight times the commercial contest. Restaurants is the module where our existing authority is closest to the volume - entity pages already rank on page one - and /restaurants is position 24.4 for its own term and 52.2 for 'des moines restaurants'.
acceptanceCriteria: Depends on SEO-021, which currently makes this page redirect away from its own canonical.
Rework /restaurants around 'best restaurants in des moines' with actual editorial picks and stated reasons, replacing the filtered grid as the primary content.
Raise internal links from 77 toward the 240 to 255 the competition runs on its hubs.

Build the cuisine and occasion pages the volume pull rewarded rather than the full taxonomy. 'best pizza in des moines', 'best burger in des moines' and 'best breakfast in des moines' each returned the 5,000 bucket at Low competition; check the Restaurant-cuisine rows for the rest.
Give 'new restaurants des moines 2026' a real hub. The plan records it at 7.63% CTR and position 7.2, the best-converting query on the site, currently served by a detail page.
Do not chase 'things to do in des moines' or 'des moines attractions' as part of this story. Index 87 is where the CVB actually is, and the plan's judgement on those two stands.
userStories.notes: This story is the one correction the volume data forces on the 2026-08-28 plan. Everything else in that document survives the new data unchanged.

userStories.title: Every event page and 70% of restaurant pages still ship as an SPA shell
userStories.description: As an AI search crawler, every one of the 525 event URLs in our sitemap serves me the homepage. SEO-001 is recorded as done and the 2026-08-31 audit in this PRD repeated that claim from a three-URL sample - an attraction, a playground, and a restaurant early in the alphabet - all of which happen to sit near the front of the render order. The build log states the real outcome: entity order is pseo(14) -> attractions(22) -> playgrounds(67) -> articles(18) -> guides(4) -> restaurants(477) -> events(525), budget 420s, and 267 prerendered against 860 left unrendered, being events 525/525 (ALL) and restaurants 335/477. Confirmed on production: /events/blue-october-foiled-20th-anniversary-world-tour-2027-03-12 and /restaurants/zombie-burger-drink-lab both return the homepage title with zero JSON-LD. The strict gate recorded 0 rejections, so nothing FAILED - the pass simply ran out of time, and the priority order makes events the guaranteed casualty. Events is the module docs/seo-plan-2026-08-28.md calls the highest-value one on the site.
acceptanceCriteria: This is a budget and ordering problem, not a rendering failure. The strict gate reported 0 rejections. Do not weaken or remove that gate while fixing this - it is the thing standing between us and 1,127 pages of boilerplate.

Do the arithmetic against the host limit before choosing a fix. Observed rate was 267 entities in 420s, about 0.64/sec. All 1,127 at that rate is roughly 1,770s for entities alone, near 31 minutes with the rest of the build, against a Cloudflare Pages build timeout of 20 minutes. Raising PRERENDER_ENTITY_BUDGET_SECONDS ALONE CANNOT FIT. Raising PRERENDER_CONCURRENCY, or rendering incrementally, is the lever.

Prefer incremental prerendering - render only entities whose updated_at changed since the last successful build - if a full pass cannot fit in the timeout. A full pass every build is not required; complete coverage is.
Whatever the mechanism, events must not be last in ENTITY_SITEMAPS priority while coverage is partial. A category that is always fully unrendered is worse than every category being evenly partial.

Verify with curl -A GPTBot against production after deploy, sampling the END of each sitemap rather than the start: a late-alphabet restaurant, and two events. Each must return its own title and at least one application/ld+json block. Sampling the front of the render order is what produced the wrong conclusion in the first place.

Add a CI assertion on entity coverage so partial coverage fails the build loudly rather than printing a warning that a passing build buries. scripts/check-entity-coverage.mjs already exists - make it enforce, or record why it cannot.
userStories.notes: Raised 2026-08-31 from the build log while verifying SEO-021, not from the original audit, which got this wrong. Sequenced ahead of the phase 2 content stories: publishing more pages that crawlers cannot read repeats the mistake at greater volume.
